title: Quarterly initiative weave and release-window orchestration for company OKRs
creator: Alex Martinez
description:
Goal: Produce a stitched company-level roadmap that maps Q2 OKRs to explicit initiative windows, cross-functional owners, and gating dependencies so that engineering, design, and GTM teams can plan commits into fixed release windows.

Why: Current OKR -> initiative mapping is fragmented across team OKRs and release cadences. Teams are building features that claim to support company goals, but we lack a single source of truth that ties initiative milestones to release windows and the infra/runtime gating work required by Dedicated/Private customers. This causes mid-quarter re-scopes and SLA/regression risks for customer-facing launches.

Scope:
- Catalog active company-level OKRs and all line-item initiatives mapped to them.
- For each initiative, define a 1-2 week release window (target week) in Q2 and identify owners from Eng/Design/Product/GTM.
- Surface infra/runtime dependencies (e.g., autoscaling policy changes, KV cache rollout, quantization testing) and flag which require Dedicated/Private coordinated deploys.
- Produce a stakeholder RACI and a gating checklist per initiative (quality, infra signoff, observability, docs, rollback plan).
- Build a weekly sync cadence and a lightweight dashboard to track initiative health against the release window (green/amber/red).

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We prioritize reliability and SLO preservation over feature scope; for any conflict we will delay scope rather than accept infra risk.
- Tight release windows increase cross-team coordination overhead; to limit this we will cluster initiatives by shared infra dependencies where possible.
- Some infra work (runtime kernel updates, batcher tweaks) introduces risk to platform latency; those items will be gated behind a canary release and per-token cost analysis.

Success criteria:
- 90% of company initiatives have an assigned release window and owner by the end of Cycle 53.
- No more than 2 production regressions labeled as Q2 OKR launches caused by missing infra gating.
- Dashboard available and used in weekly leadership syncs with actionable reds translated into mitigation plans within 48 hours.

updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff with Eng Leads (Nikhil, Sara), Design (Maya), and GTM (Jon). Agreed to prioritize OKR A (reduce per-token latency) and OKR C (enterprise adoption) for Q2 windows.

2026-02-20: Pulled dependency inventory. Notable infra items: autoscaler policy refactor (ENG-19500), KV cache TTL harmonization (ENG-19610), quantization compatibility tests for dedicated (ENG-19685). Marked these as blockers for initiatives that require Dedicated rollout.

2026-02-25: Decision: cluster three related feature launches (dedicated throughput metrics, per-route tracing, and rollout automation) into the same release window to reduce repeat canaries. Trade-off: slightly larger rollout but fewer infra rollouts overall.
2026-03-01: Design review feedback incorporated. Design asks for an additional usability sprint for rollout UX (DES-2013). Estimate bump +2 points; moved to priority for cycle allocation.

2026-03-03: Engineering raised a risk on runtime kernel selection (ENG-19821). Mitigation: dedicate a one-week kernel compatibility test window and reserve a fallback model variant for canary traffic.
2026-03-05: Created weekly leadership dashboard prototype (retained in Confluence) and scheduled Friday sync cadence. Owner assignment completed for 16 initiatives; remaining 4 need GTM owner input.

Action items: 1) Priya to finalize release windows and publish dashboard (due 2026-03-12). 2) Eng leads to provide canary plan for infra blockers (due 2026-03-10). 3) GTM to confirm owners for the four unassigned initiatives (due 2026-03-09).
risks: Insufficient dedicated capacity to run parallel canaries across regions - could force staggering of releases.
Kernel-level changes may regress latency for high-throughput customers; need robust rollback plan.
Ambiguous ownership on cross-team steps (e.g., docs + migration guidance) may delay launches.

Eng to deliver canary/runbook drafts for ENG-19500 and ENG-19685 by 2026-03-10.
